description: FrontierX is a team of curious minds brought together by a shared interest in Earth science, NASA data and technology. We are inspire by a desire to listen to Earth's changing signals and uncover the stories hidden within them. We bring together curiosity, scientific thinking and a spirit of exploration to engage with the challenges of understanding our changing planet.
summary:
Our project "Earth System Fingerprints" inspired by NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 and its challenge, “Be An Earth System Trend Detective!”, we developed Earth System Fingerprints—an interactive Earth-observation platform for investigating environmental change through multiple satellite-derived signals.

The platform brings together three key indicators: Land Surface Temperature (LST), vegetation health (NDVI), and soil moisture, across three distinct regions: Bangladesh, the Indo-Gangetic Plain, and the Amazon Frontier.

Our solution addresses four fundamental questions: What is changing? Where is it changing? How much is it changing? And is the change statistically significant Interactive maps, spatial analysis, time-series visualizations, and regional comparisons help explore these questions. Sen’s slope quantifies the direction and magnitude of trends, while the Mann–Kendall test evaluates their statistical significance.

Environmental change cannot be fully understood through a single indicator. By connecting temperature, vegetation, and soil moisture in one analytical framework, Earth System Fingerprints offers a broader perspective on regional environmental patterns. It makes complex NASA observations easier to explore, compare, and interpret, supporting a more transparent and evidence-based understanding of our changing planet.
details:
Project Overview

Earth System Fingerprints is an interactive Earth-observation platform developed for NASA’s Be An Earth System Trend Detective! challenge. It brings together NASA satellite-derived land surface temperature (LST), vegetation indices (NDVI) and soil-moisture observations to investigate environmental change across three contrasting regions: Bangladesh, the Indo-Gangetic Plain and the Amazon Frontier.

Our Solution

The platform provides a unified workflow for exploring environmental variables, examining their changes over time and comparing patterns across regions. It is designed around the four central questions of the challenge:

  • What is changing? Explore multiple Earth-system variables.
  • Where is it changing? Investigate trends across three geographically distinct study regions.
  • How much is it changing? Estimate the magnitude and direction of change using Sen’s slope.
  • Is the change significant? Assess statistical significance using the Mann–Kendall trend test.

Interactive maps, time-series visualizations, spatial analysis and regional comparisons bring these capabilities together in one platform.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Environmental change cannot always be understood through a single measurement or location. By examining temperature, vegetation and soil moisture together, the platform provides a broader perspective on regional environmental patterns. It makes satellite-derived evidence easier to explore and compare, while presenting data availability and quality limitations to support careful interpretation.

The project aims to make Earth-observation trend analysis more accessible, encourage evidence-based investigation and provide a foundation that can be extended to additional regions and environmental variables.

Technology and Tools

  • Frontend: React, TypeScript and Vite
  • Interactive Earth visualization: CesiumJS
  • Scientific visualization: Plotly
  • Backend: Python and FastAPI
  • NASA data access: NASA AppEEARS
  • Deployment: Vercel and Render
  • Version control: Git and GitHub

Creativity and Design Considerations

The central idea is to connect multiple environmental indicators, statistical trend analysis and geographic exploration in one interactive experience. Rather than presenting isolated charts, Earth System Fingerprints connects regional maps, time-series analysis and cross-region comparisons to support a more complete investigation of environmental change.

The team also considered spatial and temporal coverage, data quality, missing observations, variable-specific physical units and statistical significance.
